💡 Key Takeaways
  • Conservatives may instinctively want to push back against closer EU ties, but they have to train their focus elsewhere.
  • Anyone who accidentally switched to BBC One at about 9.45am on Sunday to be greeted by Theresa May awkwardly espousing the virtues of Brexit could have been forgiven for thinking they had woken up in around 2018 – and not being especially pleased at the idea.
  • This is one of the problems now facing May’s party.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Conservatives may instinctively want to push back against closer EU ties, but they have to train their focus elsewhere.

Anyone who accidentally switched to BBC One at about 9.45am on Sunday to be greeted by Theresa May awkwardly espousing the virtues of Brexit could have been forgiven for thinking they had woken up in around 2018 – and not being especially pleased at the idea.

This is one of the problems now facing May’s party. For all that it is a reflex action for Conservatives to push back against closer ties with the EU, Andy Burnham’s decision to pursue such a course plunges them back into their own unhappy place.

For Tory MPs and activists with a full set of Brexit campaign medals, this risks being especially triggering. May’s repeated attempts to cobble together a departure deal that could unite her party involved repeated humiliations, among them the heaviest ever parliamentary defeat for a British PM, when the Commons rejected her Brexit strategy by a majority of 230.

With the afterglow of Boris Johnson’s “get Brexit done” 2019 election triumph now seven years and four prime ministers ago, under Kemi Badenoch the party has opted to do less of the, in David Cameron’s resonant phrase, “banging on about Europe” and instead focus on policy areas such as the economy, social security and defence.

In a speech to the CBI conference on Monday, Badenoch will condemn Burnham’s upcoming deal with the EU, sealed at last week’s Brussels summit, but based on the argument that he botched the negotiations, not that closer links as such are bad in themselves.

“If we can make our trading relationship better, good. I’m all for working on a smarter deal,” she was to tell the business leaders’ gathering.

Recent findings suggest that the reasons for this caution are obvious. To begin with, even more ardent Tory Brexiters struggle to articulate any tangible benefits to the UK in the decade since the referendum, beyond slightly niche constitutional points about self-determination.

In her BBC interview, May, who comments sparingly on live political subjects despite being an active Tory peer, did not even try to argue that Brexit had been a success, instead saying it was impossible to know, given events such as Covid and Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, and then adding: “I don’t think Britain’s state today is about whether or not we left the European Union.”.

In a recent development, many voters are much clearer about what they think. Polling suggests that a clear majority of Britons view Brexit as both a failure and a mistake in the first place, with similar support for rejoining the EU, although this depends in part on the pre-conditions for doing so.

This is a product of both lived experience and what pollsters delicately call “demographic churn” – that is, the death of many of the disproportionately older Britons who voted leave and their replacement on the electoral rolls by younger people with more positive views about the EU.

A latest constituency-level poll on Brexit sentiment found that hundreds of previously leave-backing areas, including Burnham’s Makerfield seat, now support rejoining.

Of the 632 Commons seats in England, Scotland and Wales, it found that voters in 512 would rejoin the EU, with 47 too close to call. Just 73 areas – slightly over 11% of the total – still want to stay out.

It has been revealed that for the Conservatives, the battle has not ended. Badenoch will lambast the PM when he sets out his new EU deal in parliament on Monday. Her deputy, Alex Burghart, has already promised that a future Tory government would unpick it.

Industry observers note that but make no mistake, Europe is no longer the Conservatives’ defining political thread, and division, as it was for several decades. May might, understandably, be unable to move on from the glitch that made her PM and then destroyed her career. But her party, like the country, has no choice.

Ex-GM CEO on Mary Barra succession planning: 'It's going to be tough'

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Former General Motors CEO and Chairman Dan Akerson doesn't mince words when asked about the challenges the automaker faces in finding a successor for GM CEO Mary Barra: "It's going to be tough.".
  • It has been revealed that he should know.
  • Akerson said Barra will be hard to replace, citing her success and prominence as the first female CEO of any major automaker and the ongoing challenges facing the automotive industry, such as artificial intelligence, vehicle digitalization, and the rise of China and autonomous vehicles.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former General Motors CEO and Chairman Dan Akerson doesn't mince words when asked about the challenges the automaker faces in finding a successor for GM CEO Mary Barra: "It's going to be tough.".

It has been revealed that he should know. The 78-year-old businessman and U.S. Navy veteran helped with his own succession planning and recommended to GM's board in 2013 that Barra replace him as CEO. She has held the top job since Jan. 15, 2014.

Akerson said Barra will be hard to replace, citing her success and prominence as the first female CEO of any major automaker and the ongoing challenges facing the automotive industry, such as artificial intelligence, vehicle digitalization, and the rise of China and autonomous vehicles.

"It's going to be very, very dynamic," Akerson told CNBC during a phone interview. "It's going to be a big change.".

Akerson declined to discuss potential internal candidates such as GM Chief Product Officer Sterling Anderson, CFO Paul Jacobson or President Mark Reuss, but he said the eventual successor needs to be dynamic and, if from the outside, "adaptable.".

His comments to CNBC follow a Wall Street Journal report on Tuesday that GM is working with an executive search firm to identify possible outside candidates to succeed Barra, in addition to internal prospects. GM declined to comment on the report or Barra's succession.

Akerson, who came to GM as an outsider from The Carlyle Group in 2010, said selecting an outside candidate might be risky if there are already executives within the organization who have similar leadership and technical expertise.

It has been revealed that "Is there anybody in the organization that has that background that you know better day to day over a period of time? You may be taking a risk by bringing in an outsider," he stated.

The prospect of an outsider leading GM would be unusual in the auto industry, where major automakers have generally promoted internal CEO candidates, apart from periods of exceptional disruption such as the Great Recession.

Stellantis, BMW, Toyota Motor, Nissan Motor and Hyundai Motor have all appointed internal executives to their CEO positions in recent years.

Barra has stated several times that her successor and her longevity in the role would be determined by the board.

A notable influence is likely Hewlett Packard veteran Patricia Russo, GM's longest-serving board member who has been on the board since 2009 and leads its CEO succession planning as independent lead director.

It has been revealed that GM's CEO succession planning is done "at least annually," according to the organization's yearly proxy filing. That process includes Barra providing the board "with recommendations for, and evaluations of, potential CEO successors and discusses developmental prepares for these successors," according to the filing.

That is followed by board members engaging "with CEO candidates and senior management talent at Board and committee meetings and other forums to enable directors to personally assess candidates.".

When Akerson was preparing to retire, Barra was among a pool of four candidates — two longtime GM employees and two relative newcomers — who were finalists for CEO in 2013, he remarked.

Akerson noted he put the finalists through an extended evaluation, asking how they viewed GM's strengths and weaknesses, how they would organize the company, and their willingness to work together, potentially with other CEO candidates who didn't get the job.

Akerson noted the final decision to appoint Barra was done at a day-and-a-half-long board meeting in Washington. The candidate field was narrowed to Barra and former GM executive Dan Ammann, an ex-Wall Street banker who was GM's CFO before leaving the automaker's Cruise unit, reportedly over a disagreement in strategy with Barra, in 2021.

It has been revealed that "Mary's very deserving of all the accolades she's received," Akerson said. "She's done a terrific job.".

Barra has been leading the automaker for nearly 13 years, which makes her the longest-serving CEO of the automaker since Alfred Sloan retired after a 23-year career as CEO in 1946.

Akerson said he believes that, like he did, Barra will have major influence in picking her successor. He described that dynamic as integral to continuing her legacy leading the automaker.

Recent findings suggest that "This is vital. I think if she doesn't pick the right person, in four or five years from now and things are back in the trough, that will tarnish her history. But I think she'll pick the right one," he remarked.

Greater Manchester police declared a major incident on Sunday following reports of concertgoers reporting eye and respiratory symptoms.

One person has been taken to hospital after an “unknown substance” was let off in the crowd during a Don Toliver concert at Manchester’s Co-op Live arena, officials remarked.

Greater Manchester police stated a major incident was declared shortly after 10pm on Sunday following reports of people in the crowd at the US rapper’s show suffering from the effects of an unknown substance, which police initially believed to be teargas.

Footage shared on social media appeared to show concertgoers coughing and covering their mouths as they left the venue.

In a statement issued shortly after 2am on Monday, police said concertgoers had been safely evacuated, with several people being assessed on site for side effects.

The North West ambulance service said more than 50 people had been assessed by clinicians, with some reporting “eye and respiratory symptoms”.

“Decontamination is being carried out as a precaution and one patient has been taken to Manchester Royal Infirmary for further assessment,” it said in a statement.

“We deployed several emergency crews, including our Hazardous Area Response Team, to support the safe assessment and treatment of people at the scene.

“Anyone at tonight’s event who has since noticed side-effects or become ill should seek medical advice.”.

Greater Manchester police assistant chief constable Steph Parker noted more than 12,000 people had been safely evacuated from the arena.

“Our priority was to ensure the safety of every person that was attending the concert,” she stated in a statement.

“Several people were treated on site, and one has been taken to hospital at this time. Anyone who has left the event and since become unwell is advised to attend their local hospital.

“We understand the concern that this incident will have raised – particularly those with loved ones at the venue last night – and we’d like to thank everyone for their patience as we dealt with it.

“There were over 12,000 people in attendance during this concert who were safely escorted from the arena so they could make their way home.”.

She continued: “Our declaration of a major incident has allowed us to ensure emergency services and partner agencies can work together rapidly and effectively to coordinate a safe response.

“We will now begin to fully understand what this substance was and how this incident came about.”.

Co-op Live stated in a statement that venue bosses were working with police to identify the cause of the incident.

“Following an incident in the crowd at last night’s show, we are working closely with Greater Manchester police to identify the cause and action appropriately,” the statement noted.

“Our priority remains the safety and security of all visitors to Co-op Live, and we will provide more information once we have an patch from Greater Manchester police.”.

Toliver, whose real name is Caleb Zackery Toliver, was performing in Manchester as part of his Nitrous tour.

He is scheduled to perform at London’s O2 Arena on Monday and OVO Arena Wembley on Tuesday.

The Co-op Live arena is scheduled to host US singer Phoebe Bridgers on Thursday.

Hydropower hit record lows in the US Southwest this summer

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (535 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Technologyreview

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The US Southwest generated 28% less electricity via hydropower between April and August than the 10-year average, according to fresh data from the US Energy Information Administration.
  • Sources indicate that most hydropower plants in the US rely on dams to hold back water, creating reservoirs.
  • Residents and farmers in the US Southwest, a region that includes Arizona, Latest Mexico, and parts of Nevada and California, rely on water that melts in the spring from snowpack in the mountains and is slowly allowed to flow south via dam releases.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The US Southwest generated 28% less electricity via hydropower between April and August than the 10-year average, according to fresh data from the US Energy Information Administration.

Sources indicate that most hydropower plants in the US rely on dams to hold back water, creating reservoirs. The water can be released through turbines, generating electricity on demand. But an extreme, prolonged drought in the Colorado River Basin has resulted in dangerously low water levels in the Southwest’s two largest reservoirs, affecting the availability of this power source.

Residents and farmers in the US Southwest, a region that includes Arizona, Latest Mexico, and parts of Nevada and California, rely on water that melts in the spring from snowpack in the mountains and is slowly allowed to flow south via dam releases. Snowfall in the Rocky Mountains provides about 85% of the annual flow of the Colorado River. And in recent years, the river has seen record-low flows.

Recent findings suggest that two reservoirs along the Colorado River, Lake Powell and Lake Mead, have struggled to stay above the minimum level required for hydropower plants. At the end of September, Lake Powell’s depth was 3,518 feet, less than 1% above the level required to run the water through turbines that produce electricity at the Glen Canyon power plant. The Hoover Dam power plant requires 950 feet in Lake Mead, and that reservoir was 9% above the minimum in September.

Together, the two plants produced nearly seven terawatt-hours of electricity in 2025, enough to serve over 2 million people.

According to recent reports, low water levels have been an ongoing struggle for the region, which has been in a drought for 27 years. Meanwhile, climate change is continuing to shift rainfall and snowfall patterns across the region and around the world.

The effects of climate change on hydropower aren’t entirely straightforward globally—some regions will see more rain and snow because of shifting weather patterns, while others are likely to see less.

It has been revealed that but it’s playing a role for hydropower availability, according to one 2022 review study. Rising temperatures bring more droughts, warmer winters means less snow and ice to fill the reservoirs, and more variability in precipitation can lead to alternating floods and droughts, making the power source less reliable.

Hydropower production is likely to be at its lowest level in over a decade in 2026 and tick even lower in 2027, according to projections from the EIA.

According to recent reports, el Niño could provide some temporary relief. Sometimes this weather pattern can mean cooler, wetter conditions for the southern US. Heavy rains brought floods to the region in October and early November, and the water levels in Lake Powell rose more than 20 feet from their mid-September low. But the water is still quite low, and it’ll take much more to help reservoirs recover from decades of drought conditions.

Even as a changing climate complicates the availability of hydropower, the decline in capacity could push greenhouse-gas emissions higher. In 2023, energy-related greenhouse-gas emissions rose by 1.1% globally. A worldwide shortfall in hydropower generation accounted for about 40% of that rise, according to a report from the International Energy Agency.

Russian  ballistic missile strikes on Ukraine's southern city of Kryvyi Rih — President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's hometown — killed two people and wounded dozens of others, local officials mentioned Saturday.

The attacks come amid little progress in talks to end the nearly five-year-old war and after Ukraine, on three occasions this week, struck the Kerch bridge linking Russian-occupied Crimea with Russia.

Russian President Vladimir Putin had vowed a "painful" response to the Kerch attack, as the bridge is vital for war supplies for Russian forces in the south.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Among the dead in Friday evening's double-tap strikes on Kryvyi Rih were a 7-year-old boy and a 20-year-old woman, while several children were among the 60 wounded, the Ukrainian officials mentioned.

Several fires broke out and damage was caused to about 25 apartment buildings, a hospital, schools and an industrial facility, Oleksandr Vilkul, the head of the city administration, wrote on Telegram.

Moscow, meanwhile, confirmed a further strike on Friday night in Kryvyi Rih.

Russia's Defense Ministry noted a thermal power plant in the city was hit, along with a power substation in the region of Rivne, on the opposite side of the country.

Both facilities supply electricity to the industry supporting Ukraine's military, the ministry added.

Elsewhere in the nearly five-year-long war, Russia ​also struck a ​cargo vessel ‌near Odesa, which Moscow said was carrying dual-use goods ​for ⁠the Ukrainian military.

Eleven people, including two children, were wounded when a Russian drone attacked a five-story apartment building in the northeastern Kharkiv region, Ukraine’s State Emergency Service said Saturday.

One person was wounded in a Russian attack on the capital, Kyiv, according to the service.

In Russia, local officials stated Saturday that Ukrainian drone attacks wounded three people in the Bryansk and Belgorod border regions.

Finland, meanwhile, said it detected a drone attack on Saturday morning on a Russian cargo ship in the eastern Baltic Sea, prompting Prime Minister Petteri Orpo to warn that the war is "spilling over into our immediate vicinity.".

After damage to Russia's Kerch bridge to Crimea, Zelenskyy warned in an interview with US broadcaster NBC that the structure "will not remain standing anyway.".

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Theguardian ↗ Open Full Page

Fewer than half in UK will pay TV licence fee within a decade, report warns

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (636 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theguardian

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Analysis for thinktank points to cycle of falling income leading to lower spending on content in ‘spiral of decline’.
  • Fewer than half of households in Britain will pay the BBC’s licence within a decade, according to analysis that warns that the broadcaster’s funding is locked in a “spiral of decline”.
  • With senior BBC figures concerned about the accelerating fall in licence fee sales, the independent projections also warn that the proportion of households paying the levy will further decline to less than a third by 2037-38 should the government persist with the corporation’s current funding model.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Analysis for thinktank points to cycle of falling income leading to lower spending on content in ‘spiral of decline’.

Fewer than half of households in Britain will pay the BBC’s licence within a decade, according to analysis that warns that the broadcaster’s funding is locked in a “spiral of decline”.

With senior BBC figures concerned about the accelerating fall in licence fee sales, the independent projections also warn that the proportion of households paying the levy will further decline to less than a third by 2037-38 should the government persist with the corporation’s current funding model.

Lisa Nandy, the culture secretary, is preparing to publish proposed changes to the licence fee that will force anyone who watches a streaming service to pay it. Currently, only people who watch live TV or the BBC’s iPlayer have to pay the fee.

Projections by the respected independent media consultancy Oliver & Ohlbaum Associates point to an “unsustainable” cycle of falling income leading to lower spending on strong content that attracts audiences.

They show the BBC’s licence fee income – paid by 77% of households last year – could be worth less than half its current level in real terms by 2037-38, the next point at which the broadcaster’s funding model is renegotiated.

The BBC’s own internal licence fee income modelling is also said to be bleak, with the corporation already making painful cuts to programmes and staff.

Nandy’s proposed latest funding model, which could form part of the BBC’s next 10-year charter, is expected to be published before the end of the year.

Other more radical proposals, such as a household levy for the BBC, have already been ruled out by the Treasury as politically impossible.

Like all media companies, the BBC is facing a myriad of pressures. The costs of making television have hugely increased, while the arrival of streamers and digital platforms has transformed viewing habits.

Meanwhile, freezes to the licence fee over the past decade, as well as extra costs loaded on to the BBC by previous governments, have given the corporation less to spend.

The newly introduced independent projections, included in a report on the BBC by the Reset Tech thinktank, show why the broadcaster’s leadership and ministers accept that the status quo cannot continue.

The study suggests the BBC’s spending on TV content will more than halve by the next charter review. BBC viewing per person via TV sets would fall from 46 minutes a day in 2024-25 to just 23 minutes a day in 2037-38. Revenue would fall from £3.8bn to £1.6bn in real terms.

Sources indicate that the BBC remains the UK’s most-used media brand, reaching 94% of adults every month. However, the projections suggest YouTube could overtake BBC TV set viewing in 2032-33.

Sources indicate that it is predicted that more than half of households will not pay the licence fee by 2033-34. Non-payment of the licence fee has already risen from about 9% of households in 2015 to about 23% last year, and the trend has been accelerating.

Dylan Sparks, the UK director at Reset Tech, said the report confirmed that the BBC’s current funding model was broken. “The BBC is critical national infrastructure and it deserves a long-term settlement that ensures it not only survives but thrives in the decades to come,” he said.

“We urge the government to defend this vital British asset and to use the BBC charter renewal process to come forward with a fresh funding model that is universal, affordable and sustainable.”.

A BBC spokesperson said: “We have consistently argued that the current funding model is not sustainable and needs reform. We will continue to engage with government to secure a fresh charter that provides sufficient, sustainable and universal funding so the BBC can deliver for audiences for generations to come.”.

According to recent reports, we think the TCL QM6K is the best TV for most people. Former senior shopping reporter Leah Stodart deemed it "the quintessential beginner fancy TV": a nice QLED model with adequate brightness, deep blacks, great color, and a high-enough refresh rate for gaming, but a reasonable price tag. (Every size is usually on sale for well under $1,000 — even the huge 85-incher.) It's primo "for casual home theater purposes," Stodart wrote. Read our full review of the TCL QM6K.

Sources indicate that there are plenty of ways to trick out a newly introduced iPhone. Moft’s cult-favorite, origami-styled phone stand is a great tech stocking stuffer that magnetically snaps onto the back of a phone and folds into three viewing positions. A built-in sleeve holds up to two cards, giving you some on-the-go and on-the-desk swagger. It's compatible with all MagSafe iPhones (and Android devices with magnets), making it one of the best Christmas gifts under $50.

It has been revealed that birdbuddy's smart feeders are super popular Christmas gifts, and the brand just came out with two latest models: the Birdbuddy Nook and Birdbuddy Home. Henschel tested them and prefers the Home because it has a larger seed reservoir and two built-in solar panels. However, the small, affordable Nook is "ideal for tight spaces like balconies and patios," she stated. Both feeders are super easy to set up and have an upgraded, scratch-resistant camera with AI-powered bird species recognition.

This fall, Apple came out with its first-ever smart display, the HomeView. Parents can use it for FaceTime calls, sending messages, listening to music, catching up on reveals, and answering questions or controlling other smart home devices via Siri AI. It also doubles as a digital picture frame. (Like Amazon's Echo Show devices, it's basically an all-in-one hub.) Up to six people can set up their own profiles on it, so it's well-suited for bigger households. Read our first impressions of the Apple HomeView.

It has been revealed that editor's note: Check the delivery times for this popular upcoming product to ensure it arrives before Christmas. You can also look for it at the Apple Store if it's backordered at Amazon.

If your family is spread out in different states, then a digital picture frame lets mom, dad, or your grandparents keep track of the entire family — no matter where they are. Everyone in the family can add upcoming pictures remotely, and their picture frames will show a slideshow of your latest adventures.

In a recent development, classic board games stir up sweet family memories. WS Games leans into that with its vintage-inspired collection. Battleship, Candy Land, Clue, Monopoly, Risk, Scrabble, and numerous other classics receive a bookshelf-worthy makeover. Each edition has a hardcover-style design and interior storage for the pieces, so it can sit proudly on a bookshelf instead of being tucked away in a closet.

Recent findings suggest that what are the best Christmas gifts for men, you might be wondering? We have a whole separate list of gift ideas for guys, but to make things quick, Breeo's USA-made fire pits rock.

They're smokeless, capable of providing hours of entertainment, and available in stainless or corten steel finishes, the latter of which develops a rustic patina over time. Breeo also sells a lot of accessories for its fire pits, including a Heavy Duty Fire Poker — another one of our go-to unique gifts for men. It has the feel and heft of a harpoon, and it can shift logs around until you have the perfect blaze.

The best robot vacuum and mop combos can take two chores off Mom and Dad's plates — a priceless Christmas gift, if you ask us. Out of all the latest models that Stodart tested this year, she thought the Eufy C28 was the best affordable option. Additionally, its "AI-powered small obstacle avoidance will reliably avoid toys, cords, laundry, or whatever else you didn't have time to tidy up," Stodart said. Read our full review of the Eufy Robot Vacuum C28.

There is something so luxurious about a brand-newly introduced set of bath towels that all match and feel wonderful. It's like a warm hug each time you get out of the shower. Brooklinen's are particularly loved by our staff — tech editor Werth said, "I firmly believe that Brooklinen's Super-Plush towels are the best towels in the world, period. They're insanely fluffy yet dry faster than you expect.".

Industry observers note that whiskey drinkers have specific tastes. Unless you know exactly what they want, then let Flaviar’s 2026 advent calendar do the choosing. This year’s edition hosts 24 great-tasting whiskies from around the globe. Each box comes with guided stories, tasting notes, and digital content for every reveal. Pricewise, it costs less than many Pappy Van Winkle releases.

For the right kind of dad (or a very cool mom), it's a gift he'll really appreciate — just be sure to give it to him at Thanksgiving so he has time to savor each day's release.

According to recent reports, there's a non-zero chance that your parents, like so many other homeowners with a little disposable income, have procured a 12-foot skeleton from the Home Depot within the last few years. (It can talk now, in case you didn't hear.) If that's the case, this custom Santa costume will give them an excuse to leave it up through the holidays. We won't tell their HOA if you won't.

Apple’s flagship headphones have never been cheap, but thanks to Black Friday sales, the holiday shopping season is your chance to score a pair at a discount — or hope someone especially generous puts them under the tree. This time of year, they're often marked down as low as $449.

Industry observers note that beyond the price, the Apple AirPods Max 2 are an upgrade from the original, boasting the H2 chipset for enhanced active noise cancellation and integrated smart audio features such as Adaptive Audio and Conversational Awareness. They also support true lossless audio over USB-C connection to hear more detail and nuance from Apple Music tracks. Read our full review of the Apple AirPods Max 2.

It has been revealed that the travel-friendly Anker Prime Power Bank packs enough power to charge an entire laptop on the go, and it's an incredibly practical gift for anyone with a lot of devices to keep charged (i.e. everyone). Wherever you are, this portable power bank can charge a laptop, a handheld gaming console, and a smartphone — all at the same time.

DJI is best known for its drones, but don't sleep on its creator-friendly cameras and microphones, either. The DJI Mic Mini has a cult following among TikTokkers, and it's a personal favorite of our own reporters. Compatible with both iPhones and Androids (plus a host of cameras), these are the exact microphones that the Mashable social team uses at events such as VidCon. Read our full review of the DJI Mic Mini.

It has been revealed that the Mashable Choice Award-winning Insta360 Luna Ultra is a new 8K gimbal camera with dual lenses and a detachable two-inch touchscreen for remote operation. Mashable assistant editor Amanda Yeo thought the latter was a really neat feature: It "turns the Luna Ultra from a nifty handheld camera into a super flexible vlogging tool that can capture more angles with ease, and is particularly attractive for solo shooting," she wrote. It's a solid investment for any aspiring or professional creator. Read our full review of the Insta360 Luna Ultra.

In a recent development, the Octobuddy is a colorful silicone suction mount that lets you stick your phone onto any smooth surface for impromptu videos. TikTok-obsessed teens will undoubtedly appreciate its simple design that makes filming GRWM videos and dance challenges way easier. We frequently see the Octobuddy mentioned in our In My Bag creator interview series.

It has been revealed that the latest installment in the Grand Theft Auto series has been 13 years in the making, and we're not being dramatic when we say it's the most anticipated video game of all time. Its story will follow a criminal couple through the streets and swamps of Leonida, a fictional version of Florida. If its soundtrack is anything to go by, it'll be a banger. If you preorder GTA 6 before launch day on Nov. 19, your giftee will get bonus vehicle, weapon, and character cosmetics.

The secret ingredient to some of the very best gifts of 2026? Pure, unadulterated nostalgia.

In a recent development, for its latest remake, Nintendo modernized 1998's Ocarina of Time with better visuals and physics, fresh voice lines, a fresh score, and free camera controls. According to Mashable tech reporter Alex Perry, who got to play the game for an hour at a press preview event, it's a thoughtful update of a stone-cold classic. "It isn't the same as a brand new Zelda for [the Nintendo] Switch 2," he wrote, "but it'll do until the time comes." It's out Nov. 5, and you can preorder it now.

It has been revealed that clips of Pokopia gameplay went massively viral this spring, and for good reason. It's "Pokémon meets Minecraft, with a delightfully goofy premise and the potential for lots of town-building fun to be had either by yourself or with a group of friends via online play," Perry wrote. It's such a good game that a lot of people upgraded to the Nintendo Switch 2 just to play it. Read Mashable's full review of Pokémon Pokopia.

Sources indicate that perry called the Nintendo Switch 2 "a fabulous follow-up to an all-time legend." It won a Mashable Choice Award for its upgraded system software and great online social features. Perry also loved its latest magnetic Joy-Con 2s, which are bigger and more satisfying to use than the original Switch's controllers. We think it's the best handheld gaming console to buy in 2026, even after a price hike. Read our full review of the Nintendo Switch 2.

According to recent reports, lego had retro gamers tweaking last year with its awesome Game Boy replica. For its encore, the iconic toy maker jumped a few gaming generations ahead, creating this Sony PlayStation set in celebration of the system’s 30th anniversary. It’s an awesome recreation of the original and features customizable details paying homage to two classic launch titles: Ape Escape and Gran Turismo. One look is enough to bring back 32-bit-era memories.

For gamers who are spending the entire winter playing GTA 6 in an old, out-of-date wireless headset, we have an upgrade option for you. The new Sony Inzone H9 II Wireless Noise-Cancelling Gaming Headset works for consoles and PC gamers, and it has the same incredible drivers as the new Sony XM6 ANC headphones.

Industry observers note that the sixth installment in Sarah J. Maas' hit romantasy series, A Court of Thorns and Roses, arrived this October, and no self-respecting BookTok member should miss it. If you really want to earn brownie points with your bibliophilic giftee, preorder them a copy of the next book, which is set for release in January. Both are available in hardcover, paperback, audiobook, and Kindle e-book formats.

Industry observers note that amazon redesigned its Kindle e-readers for 2026 with fun newly introduced colors (ube! seaglass green!) and thinner, lighter form factors. After testing the updated base model, Mashable's Mangino crowned it the best budget e-reader. "What truly makes it stand out is just how lightweight it is," she wrote — at six inches and half a pound, it's excellent for travel. Read our full review of the new Amazon Kindle.

In a recent development, however, if you have a little more wiggle room in your gifting budget, Mangino thinks the fresh Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition is the best Kindle overall: It's waterproof, longer-lasting, and equipped with an adjustable warm light. Read our full review of the Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition.

Recent findings suggest that psst: Don't forget to remove the Kindle lockscreen ads before you gift. To quote our tech editor, "it's borderline rude" not to.

Amazon's first page turner, the Kindle Click, "will level up your cozy evenings spent reading," said Mangino, and it's a must-have for the BookTok set. It lets you turn the pages of a Kindle or adjust its brightness when you're snug under the covers of your fuzziest blanket. (It's compatible with models from 2024 onward.) Unlike other page-turners we've tried, it works via Bluetooth. Read our full review of the Amazon Kindle Click.

According to recent reports, A gooseneck stand is a "luxury" for any regular e-reader user because it situates the device "within reading distance without any arm fatigue," Mangino noted. Based on her testing, this Magipea model works nicely with both Kindle and Kobo models. The best tech deal this week The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

In a recent development, trivia night at the local bar is fun, but hosting one at home can be even better. Hitster is an icebreaker that gets everyone working together to identify hit songs from the past century. Scan a card to play a track, then guess the year it was released. Themed editions — including All American, Guilty Pleasures, and Latino —broaden playability and let you tailor the music to your manufacturer.

Multiple Mashable editors and writers swear by Loop's earplugs, which look like jewelry, fit comfortably in most people's ears, and make a unique stocking stuffer. The Loop Experience 2 are great for regular concert- and music festival-goers; Mashable's Henschel even wore them to a Beyoncé show. "I could hear Beyoncé and her band perfectly, but the din of the stadium was almost completely suppressed," she wrote. They come in a range of color options, including some limited-edition metallic variants designed in partnership with Harry Styles.

This spring, Sony launched some new Bluetooth record players for the first time in seven years. Henschel tried the entry-level PS-LX3BT model and called it "a stylish turntable with idiot-proof plug-and-play functionality." She pointed out that it has a USB-B port in the back, which you can use to rip vinyl tracks onto a laptop. If your partner collects vinyl, this is one of those Christmas gift ideas they'll appreciate for years to come. Read our full review of the Sony PS-LX3BT.

CDs are the latest retro tech to have a resurgence among Gen Z. Tracking down a cool old CD player on eBay will earn you a lot of cred, but if you don't want to go through the trouble, this see-through model from Retradisc looks really, really cool. It works with wired or wireless headphones, and best of all, it doesn't cost as much as Sony's upcoming gold-plated Walkman.

Technics continues to make a strong impression in the wireless audio market. When it comes to hi-fi headphones, the new EAH-A1000 are a sonic stunner that put many category leaders to shame. They crush the AirPods Max 2 in most areas and rival the Sony WH-1000XM6 sound quality, while also outlasting both competitors in playtime (up to 45 hours per charge) and multi-point pairing. Plus, the elegant craftsmanship is a 10/10. Every audiophile should have this at the top of their wish list this year.

According to recent reports, sonos has long been a go-to for WiFi speakers, but JBL’s new Cove Series is a true competitor that offers a compelling wireless audio experience at a more attainable price. If you have someone on your shopping list who loves music, the Cove speaker will fill up their bedroom, living room, or back patio with big sound.

Plus, it even offers automatic self-tuning, AI Sound Boost technology that optimizes audio for listening environments, and hands-free Alexa voice control.

Choosing a signature scent for your hubby isn’t as easy as picking out a video game; you need to know their olfactory preferences. If you’re unsure what they like — or shopping for someone especially particular — let them decide with one of Fulton & Roark’s discovery sets. The variety gives them a chance to explore different scents and narrow down their next go-to fragrance. (Pro tip: We like Palmetto and Ghost Trees.).

Harry’s has something for every man’s mug. Guys who prefer a clean-shaven look can reach for the brand’s shaving kit, which includes the popular Truman handle with secure grip and multiple five-blade cartridges that deliver close shaves. No-shave November devotees can keep their mane well-kempt with the beard wash and conditioning spray bundle.

According to recent reports, every well-groomed gentleman deserves a luxury electric shaver in his life. The Panasonic Arc5 Pro is our pick for its comfortable, close shaves and flexible head, which is designed to improve cutting performance. It works for both wet and dry shaving, and the built-in pop-up trimmer provides seamless control and navigation to clean up edges around the neckline.

According to recent reports, we think the Mashable Choice Award-winning Shark CryoGlow is the best red light mask you can buy right now (and one of the best Christmas gifts for women). It provides more complete coverage than other masks from brands like OmniLux or CurrentBody, and each bulb can emit red, blue, or near-infrared light.

Recent findings suggest that former senior shopping reporter Leah Stodart was convinced that the CryoGlow’s bacteria-killing blue light setting is what finally cleared a year’s worth of her relentless adult acne. Some cooling under-eye pads complete this luxurious self-care device. Read our full review of the Shark CryoGlow.

Industry observers note that several Mashable staffers use Shark's FlexStyle multi-styler on a regular basis. (Mangino did her wedding hair with it!) It costs half as much as Dyson's iconic Airwrap but works just as well, if not better. It supports a ton of different attachments and has a unique twisting base that functions like a regular hair dryer on its own. Read our full review of the Shark FlexStyle.

Routine can give children structure and help them feel more secure. The Skylight Buddy guides kids through mornings, afternoons, and bedtime, while helping them develop healthy habits and independence. They can add and check off chores, events, and tasks. This digital calendar also functions as an alarm clock and nightlight, signaling wake-up and sleep times. Personalization features help families reinforce goals and daily commitments.

It has been revealed that the Playground is a cubic gaming console designed for playing family-friendly games with motion controls — no need for a traditional gamepad. Perry described it as "a spiritual successor to the old Xbox Kinect." If this is the first time you're hearing of it, get with the program: It managed to outsell the PlayStation 5 on Black Friday 2025, and was difficult to find in stock during the holiday season last year. If you proposal on gifting it within the coming weeks, we'd recommend adding it to your cart ASAP.

Since the viral NeeDoh toys are sold out everywhere, again, we have another viral children's toy that's selling out fast. Kids are obsessed with the colorful and addictive Clickeez keyboard, and you can still find them in stock if you hurry (Amazon is backordered until after Christmas, but Walmart has them).

According to recent reports, like wired earbuds, CD players, and other items from your childhood, Pokémon cards are so incredibly back — and dare we say, bigger than ever. The Pokémon TCG: 30th Celebration Elite Trainer Box is a giftable bundle that includes 9 booster packs and plenty of other goodies. Amazon is also selling it on an invite-only basis; try your luck because it's well under market price, as of this writing.

Do you want to inspire a love of music in your kids? The Fender x Loog electric guitar has been reimagined for little hands. The 3-string design is also more kid-friendly, and it comes with chord flashcards so kids can learn to shred. If you've always wanted to have the coolest kid, niece, or nephew on the block, then now you know what to get them for Christmas.

Industry observers note that we recently named the Toniebox 2 one of Mashable's Gifts of the Year in our guide to the top gifts for kids. The kid-famous Toniebox is a favorite of the moms and dads on the Mashable team. Whether you're shopping for your own child or trying to earn a reputation as the cool aunt or uncle, kids and parents alike love these screen-free storytelling devices.

If your tyke already has a Toniebox, they can always use more Tonies — the little figures you put on top of the device to activate a new storytime. Bluey and Pokémon Tonies joined the party this year.

Industry observers note that another Mashable Gift of the Year winner, this portable screen-free audio player is a hit with the three kiddos of Nicole Cammorata, Mashable's director of special projects. "Compatible cards power up everything from chapter books and shorter stories to music and learning-based content," she wrote. For an incredibly sweet personalized gift, you can have grandparents, siblings, or friends record custom audio messages on blank Yoto cards.

According to recent reports, don't overthink (or overspend) trying to think of the perfect Christmas gifts for kids. Keep it simple and combine two things kids love — Bluey and slime. This slimy sand adds a bit more texture to the average slime, letting kids mold it in newly introduced ways. Even better, you can pick it up for under $15, and still have the best gift under the tree.

Gifting a pair of the best Beats headphones is a sure bet for any fashion-forward music lover. Fans of over-ear headphones will appreciate the modular Beats 360, which features a customizable design with swappable ear cushions, IPX4 sweat resistance, pleasant sound, and strong ANC. True wireless conformists can utilize the sporty Powerbeats Pro 2 for exercise and leisure; the revamped earhook design is optimized for comfort and sound performance.

Looking for the best gifts under $100? The Camp Snap 2 is one of our top picks. This screenless digital camera has six built-in filters and super simple controls. To transfer its photos to your phone, all you need is a USB-C cable. Mangino brought a Camp Snap 2 on her Grecian honeymoon this past summer, "and now I have the sweetest photos to look back on," she said. Read our full review of the Camp Snap 2.

Pimple patches are the kind of genius idea we wish was available when we were teenagers. They turn breakouts into a fashion moment. We can also recommend Peace Out's Pore Perfecting scrub stick. Both of these spot treatments will make great stocking stuffers for teens.

The merchandising gods are working their magic this holiday season in anticipation of the biggest MCU film yet: Avengers: Doomsday. Funko Pop has a tempting lineup of Marvel collectibles, including multiple versions of Doctor Doom, beloved X-Men characters, and a 10-inch jumbo Sentinel. Steve Rogers, Thor, Shang-Chi, and several other familiar faces round out the collection.

In a recent development, if your teenager is allowed to watch TV in their room, upgrade their older set to the Mashable Choice Award-winning Hisense DécoTV. The 32-inch model "is compact enough to fit just about anywhere and simplistically chic enough to fit in with just about any decor," said Stodart. It'll be perfect for their college dorm room when the time comes. As a bonus, it costs much less than Samsung's smallest The Frame TV. Read our full review of the Hisense DécoTV.

In a recent development, no one's too old for Play-Doh anymore: This summer, the modeling clay brand released its first-ever collection of adult craft kits, Blooms by Play-Doh. Each one comes with colorful, scented Play-Doh sticks that they can press and shape into a pretty floral bouquet, plus finishing spray and a clear vase. For crafty types who have grown bored of Lego's Botanical builds, this is one of our favorite Christmas gift ideas.

In a recent development, the fresh Samsung Galaxy Z Flip 8 is the best flip phone we've tested this year, and Mashable's Werth especially recommends it "for a stylish, on-trend young person." It's easy to hold in one hand, durable, and available in an extremely cute purpley-pink color. And while its camera setup isn't wildly impressive, it does take a mean selfie. Read our full review of the Samsung Galaxy Z Flip 8.

Retro tech is having another moment. Last year, cassette players were everywhere; this year, Bluetooth CD players are joining the old-school wave (there are two in this gift guide). They’re a fun pick for Gen Alpha teens who love iPods, disposable cameras, and DVDs, and you can pair it with their favorite artists' latest albums.

The Fosi Audio Merak works as a portable and desktop CD player, with modern extras including Bluetooth, USB drive playback, and one-touch CD ripping.

In a recent development, the best Christmas gift for a hostess with the mostest is a Ninja Slushi Twist. It makes delicious frozen cocktails, slushies, and milkshakes just as well as the original Ninja Slushi, but now it works faster, picks settings for you, and adds a second mixing canister. That's right: Two flavors at once, baby. It's "just plain fun, and will make your home the go-to for your friend group," mentioned Stodart, who gave it a Mashable Choice Award. Read our full review of the Ninja SLUSHi Twist.

Bless the tea sipper in your family with this flavorful collection of 18 premium blends that bring winter warmth and wellness. These loose-leaf teas come in plant-based sachets and are sourced from small-scale farmers. The assortment includes multiple varieties of black, green, mint, oolong, and white teas.

Industry observers note that the viral Ninja Crispi and the new Cosori Iconic have both earned the Mashable staff's collective seal of approval. Why those air fryers, you might ask? Not only do they crisp up food nicely, but they're free of plastics and forever chemicals. The compact Crispi is ideal for cooking single-serve meals and meal-prepping; its glass containers come with lids for storing your leftovers. The Cosori is a sleeker stainless steel model with a bigger basket and handy smart controls. Read our full review of the Cosori Iconic.

Industry observers note that A digital dosing cup with a precision scale for weighing beans before grinding is the gift every coffee drinker didn’t think they needed until now. The Subminimal Subscale powers on quickly and features a hidden LED display for easy-to-read measurements. It can handle hot and cold liquids, and its minimalist design complements modern kitchen counters.

Recent findings suggest that the new Series 12 is the best smartwatch for most iPhone customers, in our opinion. It has a faster processor, pretty new ceramic finish options, and an improved heart sensor array. Mashable senior editor Stan Schroeder has been testing it this fall, and he said the latter is "the star of the show" because it "allows for far more frequent measurements." It also "opens the door for new apps such as Readiness and an overhauled Vitals app," he added.

We loved the Google Fitbit Air when we first tested it, and love it even more after the latest revision, which supports automatic detection for up to 100 sports and tracks blood pressure trends. It excels as both a fitness tracker and sleep tracker, making it a superb gift that athletes won’t ever take off. Not to mention it’s way more affordable than the Apple Watch Series 12, Oura Ring 5, and Whoop MG. Read our full review of the Fitbit Air.

Almost everyone on Mashable's shopping team owns an Owala FreeSip, which Mangino dubbed the "best water bottle ever." The 24-ounce insulated stainless steel bottle is designed to accommodate both sipping (via straw) and good ol' fashioned gulp when tipped back. For athletes, college students, teenagers, or anyone who drinks water, we think a colorful Owala is one of the best Christmas gifts under $50. Read our full review of the Owala FreeSip.

According to recent reports, mashable tech reporter Matt Binder, a self-proclaimed "longtime soccer dad," tested the new XbotGo Falcon sports tracking camera for an entire youth soccer season this year. His verdict: It's "a smart pick for parents and coaches." Its footage is sharp, you can monitor it in real time from your smartphone, and it works with nine different sports (soon to be 12). It's a bit of a splurge, but unlike a lot of the competition, it doesn't require a subscription. Read our full review of the XbotGo Falcon.

According to recent reports, tossing the football is a holiday tradition for many sports-loving households. This year, rifle this waterproof football into your dad’s chest. Dime Labs cleverly designed its footballs with silicone grip strips for better handling, and a woven microfiber cover to survive the wettest conditions. It comes in two sizes – 10.5 inches and 8.5 inches – with the smaller version well-suited to kids practicing their quarterback skills.

It's a cooler. It's a boombox. It's both! We love the Igloo KoolTunes for its old-school design and surprisingly good audio quality. While it lacks deep bass, it offers clear, balanced sound and can get quite loud. "It's not a gimmick, but a fun fusion of summer party gear," noted Mashable's Henschel. Read our full review of the Igloo KoolTunes.

Sources indicate that if your favorite man is always lugging around beach chairs and heavy coolers, then give him the gift of free hands and cold drinks this Christmas. The Yeti Hopper M Series Backpack Cooler is discounted right now as part of Amazon's Black Friday sale, so you can even grab it on sale.

The new Shark ChillPill is another Mashable Gift of the Year winner. It's a powerful portable fan that stands out for its swappable misting and cooling plate attachments, long battery life, and fun colorways. (Justin Bieber's SKYLRK brand teamed up with Shark for a limited-edition "Heat" variant, which is long sold out.) It came in clutch for Mangino on some of the hottest days of the summer. Read our full review of the Shark ChillPill.

In a recent development, the LifeStraw is a Black Friday classic that always goes on sale around the holidays, which also makes it a perfect stocking stuffer for people who love camping and the great outdoors. You can stick one end of this straw into virtually any water source — no matter how gross — and clean, filtered water comes out the other end.

Portable Bluetooth speakers are crowd-pleasing gifts for just about anyone, from teenagers to parents, siblings, and friends. This year, we're loving the all-newly introduced Tribit StormBox Micro 3. It produces satisfying sound in a compact design, is fully waterproof, and comes in multiple standout colorways. Tribit’s speaker is travel-friendly, with a magnetic snap that can latch onto fridge doors or bike handles.

Sources indicate that simply put, Yeti's stainless steel Rambler tumblers are crowd-pleasers. They're dishwasher-safe, incredibly durable, condensation-resistant, and available in a huge rainbow of colors and patterns. Pro tip: For a very affordable personalized Christmas gift, you can customize a Rambler with your own text, graphics, and logos on the Yeti website.

Power stations can come in handy in lots of unexpected situations. From camping at music festivals to charging up your phone in an emergency blackout, these lightweight and portable devices keep you on the grid. Bluetti makes some of our favorite power stations, and the Elite 30 V2 is a good starter model.

The AirFly Pro is a cult-favorite Bluetooth adapter that makes seatback screens on older planes compatible with wireless headphones. After using it on round-trip flights between Chicago and London, Henschel stated she'd "never fly without it again." The newer AirFly Pro 2 has simpler controls, improved sound quality, and pairs faster. Read our full review of the Twelve South AirFly Pro.

Recent findings suggest that traveling abroad this winter? Take this handy adapter along. Anker’s latest travel charger works with outlets in nearly every country and can charge up to four devices at once. The voltage detection system monitors voltage, power output, and temperature in real time. All readings and charging statuses are displayed on the LCD screen.

Recent findings suggest that travel jewelry cases are both thoughtful and practical, and we like this one in particular. The velvet box comes in a few different colors, and it ensures your wife, girlfriend, or daughter's favorite rings, necklaces, and earrings never get misplaced when she's away from home. If you're hunting for one of the best Christmas gifts for women under $25, look no further.

Industry observers note that cushy ANC headphones are a non-negotiable for long travel days, and lead shopping reporter Bethany Allard thinks the latest Bose QuietComforts are the best mid-range option for flying. When she wore them on a plane, "I heard minimal engine hum and was able to completely tune out conversations from my fellow passengers," she wrote. "I also never felt the need to remove the headphones due to wear fatigue." Read our full review of the Bose QuietComfort headphones (2nd Gen).

It has been revealed that nori’s garment steamers are a lifesaver for business travelers and fashion professionals. The Cloud Max makes de-wrinkling clothes a breeze, using gentle vacuum suction to pull fabric taut for smoother results. Anti-spit technology prevents leaks and water spots, and the steamer’s portable design fits comfortably in any travel bag.

A weekender bag bridges the gap between a backpack and a suitcase. It should hold a few outfits, toiletries, and an extra pair of shoes for a two- or three-day trip. Quince’s Voyage bag fits the bill with a dedicated shoe compartment, multiple pockets, and a padded shoulder strap. It’s at the moment on sale for half of its original price, while supplies last.

According to recent reports, still looking for more great Christmas gift ideas? Check out even more of our favorite gifts to give in 2026:.

MPs urge Miliband to force UK overseas territories to publish public company registers

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Improvements in corporate transparency ‘essential’ amid ‘outright disregard for the will of parliament’, says cross-party group.
  • Ed Miliband is being urged by MPs to use his powers to force overseas territories such as the British Virgin Islands to publish public manufacturer ownership registers – almost a decade after parliament voted for transparency.
  • Ahead of a meeting between the foreign secretary and overseas territories this week, a cross-party group of MPs from Labour, the Tories, Lib Dems and Greens wrote to Miliband calling on him to mandate public registers of beneficial ownership of companies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Improvements in corporate transparency ‘essential’ amid ‘outright disregard for the will of parliament’, says cross-party group.

Ed Miliband is being urged by MPs to use his powers to force overseas territories such as the British Virgin Islands to publish public manufacturer ownership registers – almost a decade after parliament voted for transparency.

Ahead of a meeting between the foreign secretary and overseas territories this week, a cross-party group of MPs from Labour, the Tories, Lib Dems and Greens wrote to Miliband calling on him to mandate public registers of beneficial ownership of companies.

The group, coordinated by the all-party group on anti-corruption (APPG), said an improvement in corporate transparency in the overseas territories was essential after “years of broken promises and missed deadlines from certain jurisdictions, and despite repeated commitments to ending secrecy”.

They said some territories such as Gibraltar, Montserrat and St Helena had successfully opened corporate registers to the public.

But they called out the British Virgin Islands, saying it “in particular continues to let the British family down”. They mentioned the Cayman Islands has raised its search fees to “prohibitive levels”, and Turks and Caicos have introduced huge fines for disclosing information from the register which they said was “undermining the entire purpose of open registers”.

They mentioned that persistent engagement in good faith from the UK government has yielded few results, in the face of “outright disregard for the will of parliament”.

Recent findings suggest that the BVI has a register launched this year which allows people to apply for access to ownership information if they have a “legitimate interest” such as investigating money laundering. A BVI Government spokesperson remarked: “We are proud of the BVI’s Legitimate Interest Access register introduced earlier this year, which allows for prompt, proportionate access, in line with international standards.

“We continue to work closely with the UK Government, delivering a major governance and regulatory reform programme to support global efforts combatting illicit finance, enforcing sanctions and recovering criminal assets - with significant progress recently recognised by the Financial Action Task Force.”.

However, ahead of the meeting, the MPs including former Conservative Foreign Office minister Andrew Mitchell and Labour anti-corruption expert Phil Brickell are asking Miliband to lay an order in council mandating fully public registers of beneficial ownership in jurisdictions that continue to fail to meet their obligations.

They remarked it was important for UK national security “because continued secrecy undermines our ability to enforce sanctions and leaves us open to hostile state actors and criminal networks”. Second, they said developing countries continue to be destabilised and looted by kleptocrats using Britain’s own offshore financial centres to clean and stash their ill-gotten gains.

Parliament voted for open registers in 2018 and the UK government had expected public access registers to be in place in all overseas territories and crown dependencies by 2023. However, this deadline was not met.

In a recent development, while an order in council to mandate open registers was drafted in 2020, the government remarked that because there were “firm commitments” from the overseas territories to introduce public registers, the order would not be used. It said it would keep this decision under review.

Brickell, Labour chair of the APPG, stated “it should never have come to this but every year of deliberate delay is another year in which kleptocrats, tax dodgers and money launderers can hide behind a British flag”.

Recent findings suggest that “That is a stain on the reputation of our global family. This joint ministerial council must be the moment we finally draw a line under it.”.

In a recent development, mitchell, a Conservative vice-chair of the APPG and former development secretary, mentioned: “When parliament voted for public registers in 2018, it was not making a polite request. It was the clear, cross-party will of the House of Commons, and it should have been respected.

“Instead, money stolen from some of the poorest people on earth is still being hidden behind anonymous companies in British jurisdictions. That money should be building hospitals and schools. It is paying for yachts and mansions instead, and the price is measured in lives. The British family has been patient for long enough. The foreign secretary has the power to act, and I urge him to use it.”.

It has been revealed that A Foreign Office spokesperson stated: “Security is the first duty of any government. Hostile states and malign actors can exploit opaque corporate structures like those in the British Virgin Islands to hide their assets and support activity that threatens our national security. “Ministers are actively considering how best to ensure that, where the risks are greatest, law enforcement agencies have the information they need to progress critical investigations. We will continue ongoing engagement with Overseas Territories on these complications.”.

#70367. Tech Report: Best Laptops for Travel (2026): Which to Take on the Road

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (2091 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 WIRED ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Best Laptops for Travel (2026): Which to Take on the Road

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2091 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As a laptop reviewer, I have plenty of devices to choose from when I travel for work.
  • Fortunately, there are many great travel laptops, and you’ll still appreciate them when you aren’t on the road.
  • If there’s an obvious pick for the best travel laptop, it’s the Dell XPS 13.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As a laptop reviewer, I have plenty of devices to choose from when I travel for work. In some cases, my favorite overall laptop doesn’t translate into the one I want to travel with. When I’m squeezed into a plane, I’ll choose maximum battery life and portability over features like a bigger screen or more ports.

Fortunately, there are many great travel laptops, and you’ll still appreciate them when you aren’t on the road. Of the hundreds of laptops I’ve tested in my life, here are the ones I always choose to travel with.

If there’s an obvious pick for the best travel laptop, it’s the Dell XPS 13. It’s been the best compact laptop you can buy for years, and that’s even more true in its latest incarnation. The key dimension to pay attention to on the XPS 13 is the depth, which is crucial for air travel. At 7.9 inches, it’s among the smallest laptops you can buy. Those economy-class seat-back tray tables on airplanes are only around 10 inches deep, and while that’s technically enough to accommodate even a 16-inch MacBook Pro, whether you can actually open the lid and use the laptop is another question. The XPS 13 is even smaller than the MacBook Neo, despite having a larger screen.

The XPS 13 achieves this by using a 13.4-inch display (measured diagonally), compared to many of the 14-inch laptops on this list. Second, it has very narrow bezels around that screen, minimizing the device’s overall footprint. While 14-inch laptops have become more popular in recent years, that bigger display size also increases the overall footprint—and every millimeter counts when working on a plane. The XPS 13 still has enough room for your palms when typing (unless you have huge hands), and the keyboard is among my favorites to type on.

The other two major advantages for travel are weight and battery life. This little laptop only weighs 2.2 pounds, a full half-pound lighter than the 13-inch MacBook Air. You might forget you have it in your backpack while traveling.

Sources indicate that now, the XPS 13 isn't the most powerful laptop in the world—at least not the cheaper models. The standard version comes with only 8 GB of RAM and an Intel chip with only two Performance cores. It’s good enough for basic web tasks, but for real work, you might run into limitations. You can address this by opting for the 16 GB model (which keeps the price under $1,000) or upgrading to the much more powerful Core Ultra 7 355 processor. The latter is much more expensive and comes with twice the storage, but it doesn’t add extra weight or size. Regardless of the chip you choose, the XPS 13 gets absolutely fantastic battery life. It depends on what you're doing with it, but you could easily work through a long international flight without worrying about plugging in.

If weight is your primary concern, the Asus Zenbook A14 is another contender. Despite being larger overall than the XPS 13 (with a bigger screen), the Zenbook A14 weighs 2.16 pounds—a hair lighter than the Dell. That’s seriously impressive, and I still remember how astounded I was when I first picked it up. Asus debuts its “ceraluminum” material in the chassis, which gives you the sturdiness of aluminum with the lightness of plastic. It’s not quite as rigid as metal, but it’s not as flimsy as ultra-light laptops in the past.

Recent findings suggest that if you’re less worried about working on the plane and more about lugging a laptop around, the Zenbook A14 is a good choice. The Zenbook A14 has several advantages over the XPS 13 that can be helpful on the go, including built-in ports like a headphone jack, USB-A, and HDMI. If you’re working out of a remote office or presenting to a client, these can definitely come in handy. The XPS 13 only has two USB-C ports and nothing else.

Recent findings suggest that there are a number of different versions of the Asus Zenbook A14 floating around out there. I’d stay away from the 8 GB model Asus sells and opt for the 16 GB model instead. There’s also a newer model that uses the Snapdragon X2 Elite chip, but I don’t think it’s worth the extra $450—especially not for a laptop focused on travel.

According to recent reports, the 13-inch MacBook Air also makes a great travel laptop. It’s relatively small, thanks to its 13.6-inch screen.

In terms of portability, its main advantage over the XPS 13 and Zenbook A14 is its thinness. At 0.42 inches, it’s the thinnest laptop out there—and it doesn’t stick huge rubber feet on the bottom to compensate like other laptops do, such as the Razer Blade 14. You might not think thickness matters much in a travel laptop, but if you’re squeezing stuff into a backpack, every extra millimeter matters.

Industry observers note that the MacBook Neo is also worth mentioning here. It’s not quite as thin as the MacBook Air, but because its screen is 0.4 inches smaller, it has a more compact overall footprint. Battery life is the bigger issue when taking the Neo on a trip, as it doesn’t last as long as the MacBook Air or Dell XPS 13. The 8 GB of RAM limitation doesn’t affect its use as a travel laptop much, but it's something to consider for a work laptop in general. That stated, it has a very pretty screen for a laptop at this price.

Industry observers note that budget laptops aren’t typically known for being particularly lightweight and travel-worthy. Most of them struggle, especially with battery life. The HP OmniBook 5 might be an exception. You can usually find it on sale for under $700, even with 16 GB of RAM and an OLED display.

The OmniBook 5 isn’t quite as compact as the MacBook Neo because of its larger screen, but it is also half an inch thick and weighs only 2.8 pounds. The Snapdragon X Plus also delivers solid battery life, plenty to feel comfortable traveling with. It’s not a laptop without compromises (like the poor touchpad), but it comes with 16 GB of RAM, unlike some other laptops at this price. That’s a solid deal if you need something to travel with on a budget.

Industry observers note that good question. Tablets can make for great travel devices because of their size and ease of use. If you need a proper keyboard and touchpad—and the app support to handle a typical workday—you’re probably better off getting a laptop.

In a recent development, the Surface Pro 12 is the two-in-one laptop I’d recommend first. It’s absolutely tiny for a computer, even though it runs the full version of Windows 11. Even with the detachable keyboard connected, it weighs only 1.8 pounds. The only real problem with bringing this on a plane is the kickstand, which adds some extra depth. It’s just small enough that it should fit while open on an airplane tray table, unlike the 13.8-inch Surface Pro model.

Recent findings suggest that of course, that kickstand is also a huge advantage for the Surface Pro 12 if you’re using it without the keyboard. While that would make work difficult, it’s ideal for watching movies. Set this up on your tray table with some movies downloaded, and you’ll be the envy of your aisle. And when you need to get some work done in a coffee shop or at a smaller table, you’ll be happy to have access to the keyboard and touchpad—both of which are very comfortable to use. Just know that it's sold separately.

The iPad Air, paired with the Magic Keyboard, avoids the Surface Pro 12’s kickstand concern. And with only an 11-inch screen, it’s perfect for use in small spaces—with or without the keyboard (note that there is also a 13-inch version). If you can accomplish all your work on an iPad, more power to ya! The iPad Air should give you everything you need, so long as you get the Magic Keyboard. If your travels involve more leisurely activities, the iPad Air is a great device for reading by the pool or for playing games.

Industry observers note that one benefit of this latest version of the iPad Air is not only its performance (thanks to the M4 chip inside) but also the front-facing camera, which has been moved to landscape for more natural-feeling video calls. Of course, you could also opt for the 11-inch iPad Pro for extra performance (and the incredible tandem OLED screen). It’s also slightly thinner and lighter, though I don't think it's worth the significant price difference.

Industry observers note that lastly, there’s definitely room here for laptops with 360-degree hinges—a different class of two-in-one laptops. I haven’t tested a recent Windows device with this form factor that I truly loved, but there’s no question it works well on an airplane. Just fold the screen back with the keyboard face down, and you have the perfect screen for watching movies. The Lenovo Yoga 9i 14 is a gorgeous option, though it’s incredibly expensive right now. But if you can afford it, you’ll love the 2-in-1 action combined with one of the slickest designs imaginable. The Framework Laptop 12 is also worth considering. While it’s a bit thick and heavy for a travel laptop, its smaller screen, touchscreen, and 360-degree hinge make it a good option. It’s also one of the cheaper options available, and it’s user-upgradeable.

What to Look For in a Travel Laptop.

It has been revealed that whether you’re packing for a trip across the world or across the state, a proper travel laptop shouldn’t be heavy or overly large. That rules out 15-inch and 16-inch laptops, which are so big you can’t use them on airplane tray tables or at coffee shops. But even when you narrow it down to 14-inch laptops or smaller, there are three portability factors to consider.

In a recent development, when you’re on the go, you want a laptop that doesn’t constantly make you worry about finding an outlet. Bringing a laptop power bank can help, but the biggest factor in staying sane while traveling is a device that can stay on. Many factors affect how long a laptop can last, including CPU efficiency, battery wattage, screen brightness and resolution, and more.

According to recent reports, long-lasting laptops, such as the Dell XPS 13, will get you through a long flight. The processor is the main thing to look out for. Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X series of chips are battery-efficient, as are Apple’s M-series chips. Intel also has some highly efficient CPUs in its most recent lineup, though you’ll need to pay close attention to the model number, as it can vary wildly depending on the specific CPU you’re using. To dig deeper, read my extensive guide on How to Buy the Right Laptop, which breaks down different CPU options.

How Large Are Airplane Tray Tables.

According to recent reports, the size of seat-back tray tables varies. There’s no exact size because of various factors, such as the airline, aircraft, cabin, and seat. Remember: Just because a laptop can physically fit on a tray table doesn’t mean you’ll have space to open and use it. With that in mind, here are the general averages to keep in mind. Airlines do not list tray table sizes, but you can expect one in economy to measure around 16 x 9 inches, while premium cabins will have larger tables depending on the seat.

I’ve included both tablets and laptops in my recommendations, but your choice will depend on why you’re traveling with a device. If it’s for a vacation and you really only need a device to read, watch, and play on (perhaps with the occasional email check), a tablet works perfectly. Lounging with a tablet, whether on a plane or by the pool, feels much more leisurely than using a laptop. More importantly, it'll help you avoid dipping back into work mode. Whether an Android tablet, iPad, or Windows tablet, just pair it with a compatible keyboard case—and you’re good to go.

However, if you’re traveling for work (or need to work while traveling), a proper laptop will be better. The one you already have may work just fine, but frequent fliers know they prefer a more compact device. And more specifically, a small laptop with a keyboard and trackpad will work better on your lap or on small desks than a tablet.
